source.title: Refusal in Language Models Is Mediated by a Single Direction
source.authors: Andy Arditi; O. Obeso; Aaquib Syed; Daniel Paleka; Nina Panickssery; Wes Gurnee; Neel Nanda

record.tranche_reason: The paper explicitly replicates harmful fine-tuning on a chat model and measures refusal and safety outcomes; it also tests related claims with activation ablation, weight orthogonalization, and an adversarial suffix.
record.gate_note: Figure 1 and Figure 3 report intervention results for separate models, but their plotted values are not given numerically in the text. Rows use figure-only values and the paper’s textual description. The paper’s direction-selection scores in Table 5 are selection criteria, not outcome rows. The suffix experiment reports cosine similarity across layers; its refusal-bypass result is stated in text but no bypass rate is given.
record.test_reason: The study's own results bear on V5 and V1. For V5, ablating one difference-in-means direction, or applying the equivalent rank-one weight edit, removes refusal across 13 chat models. For V1, it replicates harmful LoRA fine-tuning on Llama-3 8B Instruct. Its main method differs from the originals (activation and weight intervention), so T2 rather than T1. Neither original source is this paper.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that refusal is mediated by a single residual-stream direction in 13 open chat models. Ablating it, or the equivalent rank-one weight edit, disables refusal with little capability loss. Adversarial suffixes suppress this direction, and safety fine-tuning is brittle. The base-model 'repurposing' point is an appendix suggestion, not a main conclusion.
record.recipe_differences: The harmful fine-tuning is described as a replication, using Llama-3 8B Instruct, LoRA rank=16 and alpha=32 for 4 epochs, and 243 generated harmful instruction-completion pairs. The paper’s other tests use activation and weight interventions rather than the original fine-tuning method.
record.method_sensitivity: Weight-orthogonalization attack success varies substantially with system prompt and model family; Llama-2 models are more sensitive to system prompts than Qwen models. The adversarial-suffix mechanistic analysis is limited to one model and one suffix.

fits_no_version.finding: The chat model's refusal direction is expressed similarly in base models: high cosine on harmful prompts, low on harmless. This holds for Qwen 1.8B, Qwen 14B, Gemma 7B and Llama-3 8B.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Safety fine-tuning repurposes a harmfulness representation already present in the base model rather than creating it.

fits_no_version.finding: An adversarial suffix suppresses the refusal direction at the last token in Qwen 1.8B Chat, to harmless-like levels; random suffixes do not. It also shifts top heads' attention from the instruction to the suffix (Fig 5–6).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adversarial suffixes work by suppressing propagation of a refusal-mediating direction.

fits_no_version.finding: Adding the refusal direction induces refusal on harmless Alpaca prompts across 13 models (Figure 3).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A single activation direction is sufficient to induce refusal.

record.problems: The main intervention plots do not provide numerical values in the text. The refusal substring metric has acknowledged limitations and does not establish coherence or harmfulness; the safety metric depends on Meta Llama Guard 2. The suffix analysis covers only one model and one suffix. Fine-tuning evidence is one model and one dataset recipe. The base-model comparison reports cosine similarity, not refusal behavior in base models.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant reported outcomes omitted. Figure 3 tests adding the refusal direction to harmless prompts, which does not measure any listed claim version. Table 3 and Table 9 concern capability and loss outcomes rather than the claim versions.

untested.parts: Only one model and one 243-example dataset are used. There is no sweep over dataset size, no other models, and no harmfulness grading beyond Llama Guard 2.
Entirely untested; benign fine-tuning is only cited.
Untested; no per-token KL between aligned and base models.
Prefilling and decoding changes are not tested. The suffix result is a selected example with no bypass rate.
Localisation in a sparse set of individual weights or neurons is not tested. The edit is rank-one but touches every residual-writing matrix.
Untested; no comparison of data or objectives as causes of shallowness.

missing.what: Activation subtraction of the refusal direction: Llama-3 8B refusal 0.95 to 0.01, safety 0.97 to 0.16; similar to ablation across 13 models.
System-prompt sensitivity of orthogonalized models. Qwen 7B/14B with the Llama-2 prompt give 75.5/78.0. Over 12 prompts, Llama-2 7B averages 30.0% (SD 23.3) and Qwen 7B 76.7% (SD 5.9).
Capability cost of orthogonalization: MMLU/ARC/GSM8K mostly within noise; TruthfulQA drops 1.0–5.9 points in all models; Qwen 7B GSM8K drops 6.3.

record.verdict_notes: V4 gets no verdict: the only suffix evidence is a single suffix selected for effectiveness, with no rate. Table 2's GCG/PAIR/AP/Human ASRs are cited HarmBench results and should not be rows. Comparing ORTHO against them is a method comparison. V5 fit is approximate: the study localises safety to a one-dimensional activation subspace, implemented as a rank-one edit across all residual-writing matrices, not a sparse weight subset. Refusal scores are substring-based, and the paper shows cases where refusal_score=0 but output is safe (Fig 14–15).

versions.untested_parts: The fine-tuning test is one recipe on Llama-3 8B Instruct with 243 harmful instruction-completion pairs; it does not test a range of few-to-hundreds dataset sizes or other models.
Tests one adversarial suffix on Qwen 1.8B Chat; does not test compliant-token prefilling or decoding changes.
Tests a one-dimensional activation ablation and rank-one weight orthogonalization, not a sweep over parameter counts or ranks.
Tests whether the refusal direction is present in base models; does not compare training data or objectives to establish what causes shallowness.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: Llama-3 8B Instruct, LoRA r=16, 4 epochs, 243 harmful pairs
source_check.reason: §I.2 and Table 10 confirm the training conditions and refusal 0.95→0.00 and safety 0.97→0.08 (ft-refusal, ft-safety).

relationships.condition: Directional ablation of one direction across 13 chat models (JailbreakBench)
relationships.reason: Text and Figure 1 report reduced refusal and unsafe completions in all models. For Llama-3 8B, Table 10 gives refusal 0.95 to 0.01 and safety 0.97 to 0.15.
relationships.display_finding: Removing the single direction reduced refusal and raised unsafe completions in every model. For Llama-3 8B, refusal fell from 0.95 to 0.01 and the safety score from 0.97 to 0.15.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: Directional ablation of one direction across 13 chat models (JailbreakBench)
source_check.reason: Figure 1 and §3.1 report reduced refusal and unsafe completions across the model suite; §4.1 establishes equivalence to weight orthogonalization. Table 10 confirms Llama-3 8B refusal 0.95→0.01 and safety 0.97→0.15.

relationships.condition: Rank-one weight orthogonalization, Qwen 7B/14B/72B (any system prompt) and Llama-2 without system prompt
relationships.reason: HarmBench ASR rises from DR 7.0/9.5/8.5 to 79.2/84.3/78.0 for Qwen. Llama-2 reaches 79.9/61.0/62.9 with no system prompt.
relationships.display_finding: A rank-one weight edit raised HarmBench attack success for Qwen 7B/14B/72B from 7.0/9.5/8.5 to 79.2/84.3/78.0. Llama-2 reached 79.9/61.0/62.9 when no system prompt was used.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: Rank-one weight orthogonalization, Qwen 7B/14B/72B (any system prompt) and Llama-2 without system prompt
source_check.reason: Support holds for the tested prompts, but 'any system prompt' exceeds the evidence. Table 2 tests default and omitted prompts for Qwen 7B/14B/72B; §F.2 adds the Llama-2 prompt for Qwen 7B/14B and 12 prompt conditions for Qwen 7B. The reported default-prompt Qwen ASRs and omitted-prompt Llama-2 ASRs are correct.

relationships.condition: Orthogonalized Llama-2 7B/13B/70B evaluated with default safety system prompt
relationships.reason: ASR is only 22.6/6.9/4.4, so a system prompt largely restores refusal. Across 12 prompts Llama-2 7B averages 30.0% (SD 23.3), per §F.2 text (ortho-llama2-*-default).
relationships.display_finding: Attack success was only 22.6/6.9/4.4 for 7B/13B/70B, and across 12 system prompts Llama-2 7B averaged 30.0% (SD 23.3).

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: Orthogonalized Llama-2 7B/13B/70B evaluated with default safety system prompt
source_check.reason: Table 2 reports ASR 22.6/6.9/4.4 with default prompts versus 79.9/61.0/62.9 without them (ortho-llama2-7-default, ortho-llama2-13-default, ortho-llama2-70-default). §F.2 confirms the 12-prompt Llama-2 7B mean 30.0% and SD 23.3%.

relation.reason: The study directly measures refusal, harmfulness and harmful compliance after causal interventions and harmful fine-tuning.

tranche.reason: The main experiments test low-dimensional refusal vulnerability using directional ablation and equivalent weight orthogonalization, a different method aimed at the localization question. The harmful fine-tuning replication is an additional experiment.

source_check.notes: The no-system-prompt DR baseline is not reported; 'not stated' is correct despite the pack's proposed fix. Figure-only rows are supported qualitatively; capability preservation has exceptions, including consistent TruthfulQA declines.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: Fine-tuning changes refusal score from 0.95 to 0.00 and safety score from 0.97 to 0.08 (ft-refusal, ft-safety).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: The authors state that the selected suffix effectively bypasses refusal, but give no rate (suffix-bypass).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Directional ablation across the evaluated chat models; weight orthogonalization on tested models
reader_labels.reason: Ablation reduces refusal and elicits unsafe completions; a rank-one orthogonalization edit also raises HarmBench attack success rates (abl-qwen18-refusal, abl-qwen18-safety, ortho-llama2-7-default, ortho-qwen7-default).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Llama-2 models evaluated with their default system prompts
reader_labels.reason: Attack success remains 22.6, 6.9, and 4.4 for Llama-2 7B, 13B, and 70B, respectively, and is much higher without the system prompt (ortho-llama2-7-default, ortho-llama2-7-none, ortho-llama2-13-default, ortho-llama2-13-none, ortho-llama2-70-default, ortho-llama2-70-none).

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.reason: The refusal direction is reported to be similarly expressed in base models, suggesting it is repurposed rather than created from scratch by safety fine-tuning (base-qwen18-harmful, base-gemma7-harmful, base-qwen14-harmful, base-llama3-harmful).
